Name: Fluid Analytics AI
Description:
Fluid Analytics is building the intelligence layer for water systems - from rivers and watersheds to the pipes, treatment plants, and stormwater networks that connect them to cities.

Through its platform AquaGrid, the company helps cities and industrial operators understand and manage water risk across these interconnected systems. Rivers and surface waters sit at the center of this picture: they are the source of most urban water supply, the receiving body for treated and untreated discharges, and the primary pathway through which flooding, drought, and pollution events reach communities.

Water risk is intensifying. Climate volatility is reshaping flow regimes, intensifying storms, and stressing watersheds. Aging pipes leak, overflow, and fail. Pollution moves through river systems faster than monitoring programs can track it. Yet the data needed to anticipate these risks remains scattered across SCADA systems, sampling reports, sensor feeds, and regulatory filings - rarely brought together into a coherent operational view.

AquaGrid changes that. It provides continuous, system-level visibility into the health and behavior of water networks and the rivers they depend on, giving operators early awareness of flooding risk, infrastructure deterioration, pollution events, and emerging public-health signals before they escalate.

To date, the Fluid Analytics platform has delivered continuous risk visibility across water systems carrying more than 820 million gallons (3.1 billion liters) of daily flows, supporting early detection of pollution events, floods, and infrastructure failures.

Fluid Analytics partners with industrial operators, cities, and engineering firms worldwide to move water risk management from reactive to predictive, watershed-to-tap intelligence.

The platform supports the harmonization and standardization of bond reporting, enabling issuers to disclose the use of proceeds and environmental and social impacts in a consistent and comparable manner. The GBTP is free of charge and serves as a benchmark for best-practice disclosure, offering practical support to all market participants:

- Issuers: a simple, standardized format to report on the use of proceeds and impacts of their bonds.
- External reviewers: a clear and structured way to present pre- and post-issuance reviews and their conclusions.
- Investors: access to credible, comparable data to support evidence-based investment decisions.
- Public sector authorities: an evidence-based data tool to inform discussions on taxonomies, standards and market development.

By improving data availability and market visibility, the GBTP contributes to the development, integrity and credibility of sustainable bond markets in the region.

Name: SOSCHI Project UK
Description:
Standards for Official Statistics on Climate-Health Interactions (SOSCHI)

SOSCHI is a four-year collaborative project launched in 2022 and funded by Wellcome (Grant number 224682/Z/21/Z). It is the first initiative dedicated to developing official statistics that measure the impact of climate hazards on human health.
The project aims to establish a statistical framework and unified methods for official reporting, while also creating a global reporting and knowledge-sharing platform. This platform will include an open-source toolset aligned with the framework.
By working together, we believe we can make a meaningful contribution to understanding and addressing the health implications of climate hazards.

Description:
Event sustainability programs fail for one reason: they were designed for the Olympics, not for business events.

The frameworks that most planners are handed — ISO 20121, generic carbon calculators, self-reported checklists — were built for mega-events with billion-dollar budgets, unified governing bodies, and government mandates. They were then applied wholesale to corporate conferences, association meetings, and tradeshows run by planning teams on restricted budgets with clear business purposes.
The result: unfair liability, unfunded documentation work, and adoption rates that have barely moved in 14 years.

Green Analytics was built in Las Vegas — the heart of the global events industry — to fix that.

Our model measures what business events actually control: contracted spaces, production materials, energy consumption, and transportation. We separate organizer liability from attendee travel (which belongs to employers under Scope 3.6) and from exhibitor operations — so the report reflects what you actually own, not a blended number that makes you responsible for thousands of decisions you never made.

What makes the model work financially:
Assessment fees are distributed across attendees and exhibitors — organizers typically complete their Tier One Assessment at $0 out-of-pocket. A portion of every assessment funds the Event Carbon Reduction Fund, returning implementation money directly to the event. Planning teams receive a 5% commission on assessment revenue for documentation coordination — the first framework that pays planners for sustainability work rather than adding it as unfunded overhead.

Aligned with EIC Sustainable Event Standards, the NZCE Roadmap, and GHG Protocol Scope 3.6. Based in Las Vegas. Supporting major U.S. event markets.


The free ebook — How to Host a Zero Emission Business Event and Get Paid for It — is at GreenAnalytics.org.

We specialize in providing customized dashboards, predictive modeling, geospatial analysis, and decision intelligence across key sectors such as agriculture, aquaculture, climate, energy, and social development. Name: The City Sponge
Description:
On the surface, The City Sponge is a newsletter about helping people in NYC with flooding info and tips on how they can be more resilient, from the basement to the broader community.  But that topic can easily overwhelm people with many sub-topics and deter them from taking action.  And it is action between the storms that leads to resilient cities. 
So the big idea is chunking up the various aspects into smaller digestible stories: from waterproofing your home to sewer connections and stormwater management, from insurance and real estate laws to return on investment, from feeling overwhelmed to feeling engaged and supporting good policies.  And these stories generate a list of willing consumers who need help making the journey to resilient practices.  Along the way we leverage AI tools for solution QA and assessment on local regs, vendor selection, or risk.  The audience and data can be used for market research about the sector.  And the dialogue can provide community engagement on larger public projects or even policy changes.  In this way, The City Sponge is starting small but aims to be a larger platform for resiliency education and action, helping consumers learn to live with more water, and helping the industry and government learn how to engage them.  If we can make it work here (NYC) then....you know the song.

Name: Enterprise Neurosystem
Description:
The Enterprise Neurosystem is an open-source artificial intelligence (AI) research community, founded on the guiding belief that all species and ecosystems on Earth are interconnected within a single, unified system. Humanity’s unprecedented impact on this system necessitates a bold and collaborative response.

To meet this challenge, a global-scale AI network is urgently required - one that integrates the vast array of satellites, sensors, and data sources that currently operate in isolation.  By unifying these resources, the Enterprise Neurosystem aims to unlock powerful AI-driven analytical capabilities, enabling a deeper understanding of the root causes and systemic conditions underlying today’s environmental crises.  Through this open and collaborative framework, the community will generate actionable insights, course-correction strategies, and solution pathways to address the escalating climate emergency.

The initiative is supported by more than 190 volunteers from over 30 companies and academic institutions. These contributors generously dedicate their time and expertise to this nonprofit effort, representing organizations such as Stanford SLAC, CalTech, UC Berkeley, EY, IBM Research, NVIDIA, Meta, Red Hat, Reliance Jio, Verizon, and Yahoo!.

The Enterprise Neurosystem actively supports developing nations and collaborates with major international bodies, including the UNFCCC Technology Executive Committee (TEC), the Climate Technology Centre and Network (CTCN), and AIM for Climate—the global initiative for climate-smart agriculture and food systems, jointly sponsored by the United Arab Emirates and the United States. And in addition to direct enablement, the community hosted the UNFCCC TEC AI Innovation Grand Challenge in 2024, which included AI technology proposals from entrepreneurs and academics from over 60 countries, largely from developing nations (https://unfccc.int/ttclear/events/2024/2024_event04).

Name: Possibility Ocean

Our proprietary data platform provides continually updated research alongside data-backed communications insights that enable companies to better market their climate actions and products, increase revenue and strengthen their brand.

Description:
Resilient Analytics, A Stanley Consultants Company, brings 20 years of experience in assessing climate impacts and developing resiliency strategies to support infrastructure efficiency and longevity. With a proven track record of successful projects for organizations including the EPA, the World Bank, state departments of transportation, metropolitan planning organizations and municipal governments, our work spans all 50 U.S. states and more than 100 countries worldwide. This global perspective enhances the localized, data-driven solutions we provide.  

Our proprietary tool set, refined over 20 years of rigorous academic and resilience planning, provides an optimized and efficient framework for delivering actionable results. We help clients identify vulnerabilities, prioritize critical infrastructure, and implement asset management strategies that protect essential services, and support public safety and economic continuity.

Description:
The Global Center for Climate Change and Transboundary Waters (GCTW) leads innovative research to understand and generate resilience to water crises in transboundary regions. Description: Cooler is a for-profit social venture that enables businesses and people to eliminate the global warming impact of their everyday purchases and activities. By connecting everyday shopping behavior to real reductions in pollution, we make it easy for businesses to answer consumer demand for action on climate change. Name: Global Solutions Alliance
Description:
The Global Solutions Alliance (GSA) is an international nonprofit organization (based in the USA) composed of individual and organizational stakeholders aligned around a commitment to collective impact and creating holistic models to inspire and inform action. Through comprehensive, scientific data-driven tools collaboratively designed for use by policy makers, investors, NGOs and other on-the-ground decision-makers, change agents will be able to accelerate their work to solve global warming and secure reliable prosperity for communities in mutually beneficial relationships with the natural environment. 

The GSA originated from the recognition that cooperation and collaboration in a system are integral to creating conditions for life to thrive. Rather than reinventing the wheel, which only stagnates implementation, leads to confusion, and slows progress, the GSA is an evolving ecosystem of partners that are committed to working together in mutually beneficial ways that support the emergence of regenerative economic and social systems. Addressing the global emergencies of warming, climate chaos, ecocide and species extinction requires humanity to move beyond siloed-thinking and work in-parallel towards a future that benefits all. 

Our collective work always begins with rigorous research and analysis to identify the most impactful systemic solutions benefitting people and the planet. The GSA ecosystem of organizations, researchers, and contributors work together to create and maintain a solutions-orientated knowledge commons and accompanying tools hosted on the Solutions Collaboratory (‘Collaboratory’): a free and open source digital public good designed by and for the planet’s solutionists.

Name: WeatherDataAI
Description:
Weather Data AI is an online data acquisition service that provides customized global daily weather data, offering historical, current, and forecasted geophysical information to businesses, developers, and individuals. Their extensive dataset includes variables such as temperature, precipitation, wind, solar radiation, and soil moisture, covering over 250 countries with a spatial resolution of approximately 28 km2 (17 square miles). The data spans from 1940 to 2024, encompassing more than 31,000 days.

To compile this comprehensive dataset, Weather Data AI assimilates raw data from various government sources, private weather networks, and earth observation platforms into proprietary numerical weather prediction (NWP) models. These models are further refined using advanced artificial intelligence technologies to ensure high-resolution, reliable global weather data.

Users can customize their data orders by selecting specific countries, variables, and timeframes through an easy-to-use interface. The ordered data is processed and delivered in CSV format, accessible via a secure, password-protected Dropbox link within 15 minutes. For more information or to place an order, visit their website at https://weatherdata.ai/

Name: New York State Mesonet
Description: In April 2014, the State of New York in collaboration with the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services funded the University at Albany to design, install, and operate the NYS Early Warning Weather Detection System. The centerpiece of the system is the New York State Mesonet, a network of 127 weather stations across the state, with at least one site in every county and borough. Each of the 127 stations measures temperature, humidity, wind speed and direction, pressure, solar radiation, snow depth, and soil information. In addition, several sub-networks of specialty sites have been deployed. A Profiler Network of 17 sites provides additional atmospheric data in the vertical (up to 6 miles above ground); a Flux Network of 17 stations monitors the surface energy budget; and a Snow Network of 20 sites measures snow water content. Operated by the University at Albany, the New York State Mesonet collects, archives, and processes data in real-time every 5 minutes, feeding weather prediction models and decision-support tools for users across the greater New York region.

Name: RainWatch
Description:
What is RainWatch?
RainWatch is a scalable, weather data network developed to increase grower efficiency through micro-climate analysis. Small, on-site, weather stations collect real-time climate data across farms, then communicate with each other to form an observational data network. This network improves climate-based decision-making, showing optimal times to irrigate, harvest, or protect crops and also creates a micro-climate data layer that will enhance national forecasting models from agencies like NOAA, NWS, and The Weather Channel.
An AI-based learning system “AUSPEX” cross references local observations with public forecast models, adapting over time to each station’s unique micro-climate. While RainWatch’s primary goal is to support growers with accurate, location-specific analysis, its broader capability includes strengthening the accuracy, accessibility, and reliability of meteorological data for agriculture, education, and meteorological agencies.

Name: AtmoFacts
Description:
We are a mission-driven team dedicated to transforming the climate tech landscape. We were founded in 2023 by Dr. Stefan Metzger with a vision to harness the power of surface-atmosphere science for earth stewardship. Our flagship technology, FluxMapperTM represents the culmination of over a decade's work in pushing the boundaries of direct atmospheric eddy-covariance measurements. 

Why AtmoFactsTM Stands Apart:

FluxMapperTM is at the heart of our operation, providing unprecedented high-resolution spatial maps of greenhouse gas (GHG), water, and heat exchanges. A FluxMapTM deciphers complex atmospheric data into actionable insights, enabling precision agriculture, urban air quality management, industry leak detection, and more. 

Beyond the lab, our technologies are making strides in agriculture, forestry, and environmental intelligence. We offer a cost-effective and direct approach to emissions quantification, shifting away from traditional methods that often rely on indirect indicators or extensive manual labor. Our Surface-Atmosphere Science-as-a-Service model is set to revolutionize how environmental data drives interoperable decision-making across economic sectors. 

We are more than a service provider; we're a partner in climate accountability. From academia to industry stakeholders, we empower our clients with precise, transparent, and actionable data to drive meaningful environmental decisions. From the fields and oil wells of Colorado to the AGU Fall Meeting, we're on the ground, sharing insights and refining our technologies with the community. 

As we prepare for our public launch, we invite you to join us in making a difference. Whether you're an industry professional, a researcher, or simply passionate about our planet's future, there's a place for you in our story. 

Stay connected at info@atmofacts.com and be part of a sustainable future.

Name: AtmoScale
Description:
1,290 weather radars operate across 92 countries, generating some of the most valuable environmental data on Earth. Most of it stays locked in fragmented archives, vendor-specific formats, and workflows never built for multi-year analysis or AI.

AtmoScale builds the cloud-native infrastructure that gives institutions control of their own data — turning archives into analysis-ready cubes with Radar DataTree, our open, hardware-agnostic platform (built on Zarr, Icechunk, and xarray).

Proven, not theoretical: working pilots across 7 countries and 3 continents — Colombia, USA, Germany, Italy, Canada, Panama, and Serbia. Modernized archives cut analysis time from ~11 hours to ~25 seconds, and move up to 5.8x less data per query.

We also maintain NEXRAD ARCO, an open, continuously-updated NEXRAD dataset on the AWS Registry of Open Data.

Founded by the co-author of "Radar Meteorology: A First Course," AtmoScale is a small team of atmospheric scientists, software engineers, and cloud-data specialists who have spent careers working with this data.

Your observations already have value — let's make them usable. contact@atmoscale.ai

SolarScope Diagnostics exists because solar has a trust problem. Too many estimates don't hold up once a system's installed — homeowners don't trust the numbers, leasing companies underwrite blind, and installers have no way to prove their projections when challenged. We started by hitting this exact wall ourselves, building site-data tools for a previous energy venture and finding the data simply didn't exist. So we built the instrument that generates it.
SolarScope is a roof-deployable sensor box that measures real plane-of-array irradiance, shading, and site conditions before a system goes in — replacing assumption-based quotes with measured, site-specific proof. Don't guess solar. Measure it.

Name: Rho Earth
Description:
Rho Earth LC builds ForestCast, a forest risk intelligence platform that forecasts tree mortality, stress accumulation, storm damage, and post-disturbance recovery across 766 million acres of U.S. forestland.

ForestCast connects three capabilities into one system.

Monitor → Continuous national monitoring of canopy condition, NDVI departure, and compound stress. The current-conditions layer underneath everything else the platform does.

Forecast → Probabilistic mortality forecasts across the full spectrum of biotic and abiotic threats. Bark beetles, drought, wind, fire, and the compound interactions that drive delayed mortality.

Scenario Engine → Stress-test any county against forty event templates, from extreme hot drought to major hurricanes. Compare management strategies before you act.

The platform integrates FIA ground truth, multi-platform satellite remote sensing (MODIS, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1 SAR), ERA5-Land climate reanalysis, USFS aerial detection surveys, and a growing cooperator network of pheromone trap and pest observation data. Every forested county in the continental United States is covered, at every scale from county to 290-square-kilometer hex to 5-square-kilometer hex.

Rho Earth LC is actively collaborating with the USFS Southern Research Station on Hurricane Helene damage assessment and Southern Pine Beetle forecasting. We build for federal and state agencies, timber owners and TIMOs, forest insurance underwriters, and carbon project developers.

See the platform in action at rhoearth.com.

Working in collaboration with multilateral and bilateral development institutions, Pegasus manages two climate funds anchored by the Green Climate Fund, covering multiple geographies and sectors in the Global South. Founding Co-Chairs are Pegasus Founding CEO & Chairman Craig Cogut and Radhika Shah, who is also Co-President Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs and board member of CEGA, U.C Berkeley, and Claudia Thieme Cogut, Co-founder of Stanford Alumni in Sustainability.

Name: Beyond Carbon
Description:
Beyond Carbon takes a two-pronged approach using technological prototypes and cultural interventions because we believe that multiple ways of knowing are needed to understand, advocate for, and respect the stewardship traditions of communities on the frontlines of climate and environmental change.

Our current work has two components: (1) a data visualization prototype that explicitly connects forest carbon data with Indigenous and Local Communities’ (IPLC) stewardship practices; and (2) an immersive video installation that places different datasets into conversation with each other to encapsulate the deep interdependence between humans and our more-than-human planetary co-dwellers.

Both components are ongoing collaborations with elders, women, and youth technologists of Mekar Raya village in West Kalimantan, Indonesia; and our in-country partners Working Group of ICCAs in Indonesia (WGII) and Tropenbos Indonesia.
